summary.text: 山 is a whole-graph pictograph of mountain peaks. Its ordinary sense is “mountain,” with “hill” and “peak” also recorded; no separate semantic or phonetic components are supported.

formation.text: Pictographic: the entire graph depicts mountain peaks standing together. The paleographic record lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen forms, but does not establish a continuous stroke-by-stroke sequence.

history.text: The paleographic record lists forms across several script stages. The selected seal-style image is a modern redraw showing upright peaks joined by a curved base; it is not an ancient specimen and does not prove a precise path of graphic change.
Xu Shen’s Shuowen entry labels 山 pictographic and offers a cosmological explanation. This records a Han-period interpretation, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original semantics.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not establish the date or lexical value of the earliest specimen: a cited oracle-bone inventory number was not checked against a primary inscription image and deciphered context. The listed stages do not establish precise specimen dates or continuous graphic development.

overview.text: 山 is drawn as mountain peaks and means “mountain”; “hill” and “peak” are also recorded senses. The evidence does not pin down its earliest attested use.
